claims.text: The patient presented to the emergency department on 05/01/26 with sudden onset severe central chest pain, rated 8/10 in intensity, described as sharp and constant, exacerbated by deep breaths and movement, with onset approximately one hour prior to arrival.
Associated symptoms included mild shortness of breath; there was no haemoptysis, nausea, vomiting, palpitations, syncope, dysphagia, dysuria, haematuria, focal weakness, dizziness, or paraesthesia.
Past medical history includes asthma and seasonal allergic rhinitis.
The patient has a known allergy to pollen.
The patient reported no current medications prior to admission.
Social history indicates the patient lives alone, is independent with activities of daily living, works as an IT consultant, and is a non-smoker with no alcohol or recreational drug use.
Family history was reported as nil significant.
Initial observations on 05/01/26 at 02:10 showed heart rate 110 bpm, blood pressure 135/85 mmHg, respiratory rate 24/min, temperature 37.1°C, and oxygen saturation 96% on room air.
Initial examination on 05/01/26 revealed mild distress, mild tenderness over the sternum, palpable subcutaneous crepitus, equal air entry, no added sounds, and no accessory muscle use.
An ECG performed on 05/01/26 at 02:30 showed sinus tachycardia with no ischaemic changes.
A chest X-ray performed on 05/01/26 at 02:50 demonstrated subcutaneous emphysema and pneumomediastinum.
The diagnosis of spontaneous pneumomediastinum was made, considered likely secondary to recent coughing or straining, with no evidence of haemodynamic instability.
The patient was admitted to the Respiratory High Dependency Unit on 05/01/26.
On 05/01/26, the patient was prescribed paracetamol 1g QDS PRN for pain.
On 05/01/26, the regimen was updated to include ibuprofen 400mg TDS for pain, alongside paracetamol, with advice to avoid straining or heavy lifting.

A physiotherapy assessment on 05/01/26 at 11:00 noted patent airway, respiratory rate 20/min, oxygen saturation 96% on room air, heart rate 88 bpm, blood pressure 120/80 mmHg, and persistent mild anterior chest tenderness with subcutaneous crepitus in the neck.
Physiotherapy interventions on 05/01/26 included guided diaphragmatic breathing and pursed-lip breathing, with education on avoiding activities that increase intrathoracic pressure.

On 05/01/26, observations showed heart rate 88 bpm, blood pressure 130/80 mmHg, respiratory rate 18/min, and oxygen saturation 97% on room air; examination revealed no subcutaneous emphysema on palpation and no respiratory distress.
Omeprazole 20mg OD was started on 05/01/26 to prevent gastrointestinal side effects from ibuprofen.

On 06/01/26, observations showed heart rate 88 bpm, blood pressure 130/80 mmHg, respiratory rate 18/min, and oxygen saturation 97% on room air; examination revealed no subcutaneous emphysema, clear breath sounds, and no tenderness.
A repeat chest X-ray on 06/01/26 showed a slight reduction in pneumomediastinum compared to initial imaging.

A physiotherapy session on 06/01/26 at 12:00 noted stable circulation, oxygen saturation 97% on room air, respiratory rate 18/min, and persistent subcutaneous emphysema without spread; the patient demonstrated improvement in breathing control.
On 07/01/26, the patient reported no chest pain overnight and mild improvement in breathing comfort; examination showed no subcutaneous crepitus and normal respiratory effort.
Regular paracetamol and ibuprofen were stopped on 07/01/26 as the patient was pain-free.
A repeat chest X-ray was planned for 48 hours after 07/01/26 to assess further resolution.
On 07/01/26, the patient received education regarding signs of pneumomediastinum recurrence and when to seek urgent medical attention post-discharge.

On 08/01/26, observations showed heart rate 82 bpm, blood pressure 128/78 mmHg, respiratory rate 16/min, temperature 36.8°C, and oxygen saturation 97% on air; examination revealed no subcutaneous crepitus, clear chest, and no accessory muscle use.
Discharge planning was initiated on 08/01/26, with routine outpatient follow-up arranged in the Respiratory clinic.
The ward nurse contacted the patient's GP on 08/01/26 at 11:15 to inform them of clinical progress and discharge planning.
A final chest X-ray reviewed on 09/01/26 showed complete resolution of spontaneous pneumomediastinum with no subcutaneous emphysema or abnormalities.
The patient was cleared for discharge on 10/01/26, with no further imaging required.
